recentWork.title: A modular foundation for knowledge and document extraction.
recentWork.summary: A modular platform combines a React interface for multisource ingestion, RAG queries, and adaptive extraction with secured API and MCP access for applications and coding agents.
recentWork.detail: Adaptive extraction uses LangGraph and LangChain to build schema-driven retrieval queries for each requested field. It retrieves relevant chunks from ChromaDB, reranks them by similarity, and constructs an LLM prompt with source material. Results include the field value, supporting context, page number, and model-reported confidence. Subsequent retrieval passes target only unresolved fields, keeping repeated context and unnecessary model input down.
recentWork.outcome: Adopted as the standard knowledge-management foundation across the client account.
recentWork.intro: A shared platform for ingesting, querying, and extracting enterprise knowledge, extended securely to coding agents.
recentWork.context: Teams needed one governed foundation for enterprise knowledge, document extraction, and AI-assisted workflows.
recentWork.notes: The platform follows a vertical slice architecture: query, adaptive extraction, Jira, Confluence, and other modules can be switched off through feature flags or removed independently. New ingestion sources can be added without reshaping the rest of the system. The API supports Kerberos authentication, while the MCP provides group-authorised access through time-limited JWT API keys for Claude Code and Copilot CLI.
recentWork.recognition: Recognised in the CIO newsletter in 2026 for the template’s adoption in contract-field extraction.

recentWork.title: Taking applications from implementation to production.
recentWork.context: The dashboard gives stakeholders an application-level view of ServiceNow CMDB data across virtual machines, services, and container platforms.
recentWork.summary: Led a phased modernisation of the Python and React codebase. The restructured backend and React application are now deployed on Rancher, with scheduled data ingestion and database-backed storage forming the next stage.
recentWork.detail: The plan separates frontend and backend responsibilities, restructures the Python code, removes spreadsheet dependencies, and replaces direct consumption of generated JSON files with REST endpoints. The next stage uses Prefect flows to collect data into SQL, with the Python API serving it to React.
recentWork.intro: Building the service, improving the codebase, and carrying the work through deployment.
recentWork.outcome: The dashboard has a better-structured codebase, with its React application and Python API deployed on Rancher. The Prefect and SQL data pipeline remains planned.
recentWork.previewOutcome: Leading its transition from a coupled prototype to separately deployed React and Python services; database-backed ingestion remains in progress.

transformation.inherited: A useful infrastructure dashboard built as a coupled Python and React prototype.
transformation.reshaped: Separated frontend and backend, restructured Python, introduced REST APIs, and removed spreadsheet dependencies.
transformation.running: React and Python API running on Rancher, with the data pipeline being modernised.

recentWork.title: Taking PDF clause extraction into production.
recentWork.context: The existing Python and React application could extract clauses from legal PDFs, but code, model-delivery, and Linux runtime constraints blocked release.
recentWork.summary: Modernised the codebase, resolved deployment issues, and established a repeatable release process suited to the firm’s document-processing and model-delivery constraints. The application has run reliably on Rancher in production for about a year.
recentWork.detail: The Python RAG service uses Tesseract OCR and FAISS. OCR was adapted for Linux and the application moved onto GitLab CI. With Hugging Face unavailable, the embedding model was packaged from Nexus into the application container, resolving the application and environment issues that blocked production deployment.
recentWork.intro: Improving an existing clause-extraction application and carrying it through a successful production release.
recentWork.outcome: Successfully deployed on Rancher and running reliably in production for about a year.
recentWork.recognition: Recognised in the CIO newsletter for contributions to the clause-extraction application’s production delivery.
recentWork.previewOutcome: Legal-document OCR and RAG application modernised and running reliably in production.

transformation.inherited: A clause-extraction prototype blocked by code, Linux, model, and release constraints.
transformation.reshaped: Restructured Python, adapted OCR for Linux, packaged the model internally, and established GitLab CI.
transformation.running: A production RAG application running reliably on Rancher.

recentWork.title: From Informatica workflows to Python and Prefect.
recentWork.summary: Built a stateful plugin that assesses Informatica workflows at application scale, produces executive reporting, and generates equivalent Python/Prefect implementations. It retains progress across runs and follows internal scheduling and deployment conventions.
recentWork.detail: The plugin separates discovery, assessment and code generation into focused skills. Discovery accepts manual evidence or Informatica XML exports and records missing behaviour and unresolved references. Assessment examines complexity and commonality across workflows. Generated code follows the firm’s Python project structure and AutoSys, Rancher and Prefect conventions. Each skill’s progress is tracked in JSON so the process can continue across runs.
recentWork.notes: The discovery step keeps extracted metadata, assumptions and missing runtime details explicit. Parameter files, scheduler details, production run history and SME notes provide additional context when available for downstream assessment and code generation.
recentWork.outcome: A connected migration process with workflow findings, executive reporting, generated implementations, and retained progress.
recentWork.intro: Taking legacy workflows through discovery and migration planning to equivalent Python/Prefect code.

transformation.inherited: Legacy Informatica workflows requiring manual discovery and migration analysis.
transformation.reshaped: Built stateful discovery, assessment, reporting, and Python and Prefect code generation.

recentWork.title: Unblocking browser automation on Rancher.
recentWork.summary: Unblocked regulatory scraping when the standard Chromium runtime could not be deployed on Rancher. Delivered a Playwright-based remote browser service and connected Crawl4AI to it in Kubernetes.
recentWork.detail: The application could not run Chromium on Rancher because of vulnerability-related deployment constraints. An official Playwright container, a Helm release in the Flux tenant, and revised browser launch and Chrome DevTools Protocol settings gave Crawl4AI a working remote browser in Kubernetes.
recentWork.outcome: The team had a working browser runtime for its scraping application.
recentWork.intro: Removing a browser-runtime blocker from a team’s regulatory scraping workflow.
recentWork.proof: Blocked browser runtime → working Kubernetes service

transformation.inherited: Regulatory scraping blocked by Chromium constraints on Rancher.
transformation.reshaped: Deployed a Playwright browser service through Helm and Flux and resolved CDP connectivity.
transformation.running: Crawl4AI working against a browser runtime in Kubernetes.

The hub brings together GitLab-hosted skills, MCP integrations, and modernisation reporting. The initial ServiceNow reporting module established a base that other developers have since extended.
recentWork.outcome: An organisational prototype for finding and accessing internal engineering tools.
recentWork.intro: A prototype to bring scattered engineering resources into one place.

transformation.inherited: Skills, MCP integrations, and modernisation reporting spread across separate tools.
transformation.reshaped: Composed independently deployed modules through a configurable Vite shell.
transformation.running: A modular internal-tools prototype that other developers can extend.

recentWork.title: Reducing memory usage and response time in financial-data APIs.
recentWork.summary: Financial-services APIs processing large datasets were consuming 6–7 GB per pod and taking about five minutes for some responses. Reshaped LINQ queries and processing reduced memory to about 1 GB and response time to 40 seconds.
recentWork.detail: The APIs were loading large result sets and performing filtering and distinct operations in memory. The LINQ and processing flow was redesigned so SQL Server handled that work before returning results, large intermediate lists were avoided, and related data was loaded only when an endpoint needed it. This reduced memory pressure and removed the multi-minute response bottleneck.

transformation.inherited: Financial APIs under high memory pressure with multi-minute responses.
transformation.reshaped: Moved filtering and distinct work into SQL Server, avoided large intermediate lists, and loaded only the related data each endpoint needed.
transformation.running: Lower memory usage and materially faster endpoint responses.

recentWork.summary: Modernised a large estate of .NET services, React microfrontends, and NestJS APIs for Kubernetes, covering framework upgrades, CI adoption, build remediation, and Rancher deployment.
recentWork.detail: Upgraded .NET Core 3.1 services to .NET 6 or .NET 8 and adopted the in-house GitLab CI templates. Resolved issues in builds, SonarQube and Nexus IQ checks, and container creation, then prepared Helm charts and Flux tenant configuration for Rancher deployment. The recurring application-chart, infrastructure-chart, and Flux setup also became a guided workflow that creates, validates, and publishes the required repositories using the firm’s conventions.

transformation.inherited: Windows-hosted .NET services and a mixed frontend estate.
transformation.reshaped: Framework upgrades, GitLab CI remediation, and Helm and Flux onboarding.
transformation.running: Repeatable Rancher delivery across the service estate.

recentWork.summary: Built supported access paths for previously isolated business data: a .NET and EF Core API over legal data in SQL Server, and a maintainable FastAPI service over financial data in Oracle.
recentWork.detail: The .NET and Entity Framework Core service exposed existing SQL Server tables and views through a supported API and was carried through Helm, Flux, and Rancher deployment. The Python service established a maintainable FastAPI structure for financial data held in Oracle, giving its team a reference implementation they could continue to extend.
recentWork.proof: Two data domains → maintained team APIs

transformation.inherited: Legal and financial data without supported access for other teams.
transformation.reshaped: Built .NET and EF Core access for SQL Server, and a structured FastAPI service for Oracle.
transformation.running: Maintained APIs that teams can consume and extend.

recentWork.summary: Converted scheduled .NET console processes into long-running Solace subscribers, enabling AutoSys-triggered workloads to move from Windows servers to Kubernetes. Led three of seven migrations through production with no post-deployment defects.
recentWork.detail: Because AutoSys was not available in Rancher, a .NET bridge remained on Windows to receive command arguments from AutoSys jobs, construct messages, and publish them to Solace queues. Each former console process became a long-running Kubernetes subscriber using the in-house library built on the official Solace .NET packages. The migration covered application restructuring, message handling, AutoSys batch changes, end-to-end testing, and production release.
recentWork.outcome: Seven service migrations with zero post-deployment defects and zero business disruption.
recentWork.proof: Three migrations led · zero post-deployment defects

transformation.inherited: AutoSys-scheduled .NET console processes tied to Windows servers.
transformation.reshaped: Introduced a Solace bridge, long-running subscribers, AutoSys batch changes, and end-to-end testing.
transformation.running: Kubernetes production migrations with no post-deployment defects.
